correctness.rationale: The symmetric graph Laplacian has projectors E0=J/N and two positive nontrivial spectral values alpha<beta. Solving Ealpha+Ebeta=I-J/N and alpha Ealpha+beta Ebeta=L gives exact adjacent/nonadjacent projector entries; applying F(z)-1=-12z/(z^2+6z+12) yields the two rational entry formulas. Diagonal entries are strictly positive because F(z)>0 for all z>=0. Every nonedge entry is strictly positive for h>0. Every edge entry has the sign of 12N/p+6h+(s-N)h^2, with p=alpha*beta>0 and s=alpha+beta. This polynomial has a unique positive root exactly when s<N. Formula for that root and the equality/sign cases were algebraically checked. Standalone check.py computes and inverts exact rational matrices on seven distinct strongly regular graphs, verifying 8172 offdiagonal entries, row sums, diagonals, and parameter identities. All-dimension proof relies on the analytical identities rather than finite enumerations.

originality.rationale: The checked published primary work concerns absolute monotonicity of scalar rational functions, general sufficient positivity of Padé matrices on Metzler systems, or strongly regular graph spectral eigenvalues. These furnish ingredients but not the explicit all-SRG if-and-only-if entrywise time-step classification. The closest accessible earlier claims with the same scalar filter concern Hamming products, complete multipartite graphs, and windmills; the same SRG graph class was previously treated with a different polynomial RK4 filter. Coverage is checked by statement implication, including overlapping special cases, not merely titles; publication priority remains qualified by unindexed older literature.
residual_risks: Older unindexed research in association-scheme matrix functions or strongly regular graph positivity might formulate an equivalent [2/2] Padé transition inequality.
The full secondary literature and every unpublished thesis cannot be exhaustively screened; best-knowledge originality is not a formal uniqueness or priority certificate.

value.rationale: Entrywise positivity is a natural invariant of graph heat propagation and probability-mass diffusion; a fourth-order A-stable implicit numerical step need not preserve it. The theorem classifies the exact all-step positivity domain over every connected noncomplete strongly regular graph, identifies the sole failure mechanism and all boundary entries, and turns the issue into a simple parameter inequality 2k-lambda+mu>=N. Infinite safe Paley/conference and unsafe triangular families and the n*h_* -> sqrt(6) scaling show structurally distinct behavior beyond small examples. The exact cutoff is useful for certified positivity-safe numerical integration on symmetric graphs, not an arbitrary finite table entry.
